items.title: Reject unsupported production receipt algorithms fail-closed
items.context: Determine whether production receipt verification currently accepts serverKey.algorithm values other than ed25519. If it does, add the smallest runtime guard and focused smoke coverage so unsupported signature/public-key algorithms never satisfy production receipt verification.
items.userSees: User sees "unsupported_algorithm" for non-ed25519 receipt verification and "authority receipt signature and native bindings verified" for the valid ed25519 path.

happy.desc: Verify a production receipt whose serverKey.algorithm is ed25519 and whose signature/public key are otherwise valid -> verification succeeds exactly as before; WHY: proves the new guard does not regress the supported algorithm path.

edge.desc: Verify a production receipt whose serverKey.algorithm is missing or uses case/format variants such as ED25519 or ed-25519 -> verification fails closed with an explicit unsupported-algorithm reason instead of silently normalizing; WHY: enforces a single consistent algorithm contract.

adversarial.desc: Verify a production receipt whose signature payload is otherwise valid but serverKey.algorithm is an unsupported value such as rsa or secp256k1 -> verification must reject before any success path and must not accept the receipt due to incidental crypto compatibility; WHY: prevents arbitrary algorithm expansion and proves fail-closed correctness.

verificationEvidence.note: authority-client smoke retains the canonical ed25519 policy-discovery path where receipt verification returns verified, preserving the supported production receipt algorithm success case.

The frozen PLAN intent named ED25519 as a fail-closed edge case, but review finding B-e3d9:F-002 corrected that as over-strict. The current smoke proves the consistent edge semantics: serverKey.algorithm=ED25519 is trimmed/lowercased to ed25519 and verifies, while blank/malformed algorithm material fails closed as unsupported.

authority-client smoke rejects serverKey.algorithm=rsa and blank whitespace algorithms with receipt_unverified unsupported algorithm, and directly asserts the native verifier rejects a non-string algorithm value.

items.title: Converge supportsDryRun requirement without speculative metadata work
items.context: Inspect the old cc-learnings ToolDef metadata requirement against current COMMAND_POLICIES, command schemas, and dryRun handlers. Either implement a real supportsDryRun metadata surface consumed by help/policy, or narrow the truth source to the current command-policy contract if the old ToolDef field was superseded.
items.userSees: User sees "Gaps: 0 high / 0 medium" and no "supportsDryRun?: boolean" entry in lattice gap_analyze output.

happy.desc: Run the user-facing command/help/policy surface after the contract change -> gap_analyze and command metadata expose exactly one current dry-run contract and no longer require a stale supportsDryRun field; WHY: proves the truth source was converged rather than papered over.

edge.desc: Exercise a command that supports dry-run and a command that does not -> the reported/help-visible policy must match actual handler behavior for both, without inventing metadata for commands that lack real dry-run semantics; WHY: catches inconsistent logic between docs/policy and runtime.

adversarial.desc: Attempt to satisfy the gap by adding speculative supportsDryRun-style metadata that is not consumed by the live command-policy/help path -> verification should fail unless the surfaced contract is mechanically tied to current runtime behavior; WHY: blocks arbitrary optimization and metadata-only fixes.

verificationEvidence.note: gap_analyze no longer reports the stale supportsDryRun uncovered_requirement; the remaining high gaps are the separate CHK-003/CHK-004 authority-policy items.

verificationEvidence.command: node packages/main/dist/cli.js --root . story_reconcile --help; node packages/main/dist/cli.js --root . test_auto --help; node packages/main/dist/cli.js --root . host_install --help
verificationEvidence.note: The live help surface now distinguishes default-on dry-run (story_reconcile), optional --dryRun plus --confirm semantics (test_auto), and always-on projection-only behavior (host_install) without inventing metadata for commands that do not expose real dry-run behavior.

The requirement truth now explicitly rejects a new ToolDef.supportsDryRun field, and the code annotations/help bind dry-run semantics to existing schema plus COMMAND_POLICIES surfaces so a metadata-only fix would contradict the documented contract.

items.title: Link Authority worktree policy requirements to existing runtime enforcement
items.context: For requiresAuthoritativeWorktree and requiresCleanWorktree, verify existing planner emission, consistency checks, executor preflight, dirty worktree handling, and smoke tests. Add precise code annotations or minimal tests only where the gap is coverage linkage, not behavior.
items.userSees: User sees "authoritative_worktree_unresolved" and "dirty_worktree" covered by smoke tests, and gap_analyze has no worktree policy high gaps.

happy.desc: Run the existing authoritative-worktree/clean-worktree smoke path in the expected authoritative worktree state -> planner emission, executor preflight, and smoke evidence all agree that the command proceeds when policy requirements are satisfied; WHY: proves the documented requirement is already enforced by runtime logic.

edge.desc: Run the same flow in a clean but non-authoritative worktree, and separately in an authoritative but dirty worktree -> each requirement fails for its own specific reason without conflating the two policies; WHY: proves consistency of the two gates and their diagnostics.

adversarial.desc: Try to clear the gap only by adding requirement prose or planner annotations while leaving any enforcement path unproven by smoke coverage -> verification should fail unless runtime evidence still demonstrates fail-closed blocking for both requiresAuthoritativeWorktree and requiresCleanWorktree; WHY: disallows coverage-link claims that are host- or reviewer-opinion-only.

verificationEvidence.note: planner-unattended smoke asserts authority JobPlans emit requiresAuthoritativeWorktree=true, preserve git-status evidence requirements, and provider planned steps carry requiresCleanWorktree for the passing authoritative worktree path

worktree-policy smoke distinguishes clean missing-worktree authoritative_worktree_unresolved from configured dirty-worktree dirty_worktree, including policy-level requiresCleanWorktree=true without conflating the two stop reasons

gap_analyze reports 0 high / 0 medium after runtime annotations and smoke assertions, proving requiresAuthoritativeWorktree and requiresCleanWorktree are linked to live enforcement rather than prose-only coverage

items.title: Link planner confirmation policy to story creation blocking behavior
items.context: For requiresConfirmationBeforeStoryCreate, verify default plannerPolicy behavior and planner_create_story blocking behavior. Add precise coverage linkage or focused regression only if current tests do not prove fail-closed story creation.
items.userSees: User sees "confirmation required before Story creation" when confirmation is missing, and no requiresConfirmationBeforeStoryCreate high gap remains.

happy.desc: Run planner story-creation flow when plannerPolicy requires confirmation and explicit confirmation is present -> story creation proceeds and the policy/result surface shows the confirmation gate was satisfied; WHY: proves the intended unblock path still works.

edge.desc: Run the same flow under a policy/profile that does not require confirmation -> story creation behavior matches that policy without inheriting the stricter gate accidentally; WHY: verifies the requirement is policy-driven rather than globally hardcoded.

adversarial.desc: Attempt planner_create_story without the required confirmation while all other inputs are valid -> it must fail closed before creating the story and must not rely on downstream cleanup to undo partial creation; WHY: proves real blocking behavior instead of post-hoc remediation.

verificationEvidence.note: planner-unattended smoke records planner_answer confirmationDigest and then planner_create_story succeeds with a persisted Story id when requiresConfirmationBeforeStoryCreate is satisfied
planner-unattended smoke asserts local autonomous plannerPolicy has requiresConfirmationBeforeStoryCreate=false and create-story proceeds without inheriting the stricter confirmation gate

planner-unattended smoke attempts planner_create_story with a confirmation-required draft and no confirmationDigest; it returns blocked with confirmation required before Story creation and status shows no storyId was created

items.title: Prove gap convergence and host-neutral review evidence
items.context: Run gap_analyze before/after, relevant focused tests, and lattice validate. Record Codex host execution evidence and two Claude CLI host review attempts or availability downgrades as advisory evidence, while keeping Lattice CLI/test outputs as the authoritative gate facts.
items.userSees: User sees "Gaps: 0 high / 0 medium" from lattice gap_analyze and "validation PASS" for B-e3d9, with host reviews labeled advisory.

happy.desc: Run gap_analyze before and after the fix set, plus the focused smoke tests and lattice validate -> final authoritative outputs show 0 high and 0 medium gaps and validation passes with evidence bound to this story and HEAD; WHY: proves actual convergence instead of narrative closure.

edge.desc: If a second host review tool such as Claude CLI is unavailable or downgraded on this machine, record that availability result as advisory evidence while keeping the same Lattice command outputs authoritative -> the story still distinguishes host-neutral gate facts from host-specific advisory notes; WHY: preserves host neutrality without hiding environment differences.

adversarial.desc: Attempt to claim success using only host-specific review transcripts or one machine observation while gap_analyze, validate, or focused test evidence is missing, stale, or contradictory -> verification must reject completion and require current Lattice outputs as the source of truth; WHY: prevents non-authoritative evidence from masking correctness gaps.

verificationEvidence.command: lattice gap_analyze; npm --prefix packages/main run build; npm run test:authority-client; npm run test:lattice-cli-migration-smoke; npm run test:worktree-policy-smoke; npm run test:planner-unattended-smoke
verificationEvidence.note: Current-head convergence suite passed: gap_analyze reports Requirement coverage 100%, Test coverage 100%, Gaps: 0 high / 0 medium; build and all focused smokes for receipt algorithm, dry-run help, worktree policy, and planner confirmation passed. lattice validate is rerun after this evidence so final pass remains Lattice-authoritative, not host narrative.

verificationEvidence.command: command -v claude && claude --version; guarded claude -p advisory review attempt 1; guarded claude -p advisory review attempt 2
verificationEvidence.note: Codex host coordinated the story and Lattice commands. Claude CLI host was present at /Users/jek/.nvm/versions/node/v22.13.0/bin/claude version 2.1.88; advisory attempt 1 returned a one-sentence confirmation that Lattice gap_analyze/validate are authoritative, while advisory attempt 2 was degraded by the local 15s guard with exit 143/no output. Both are recorded as advisory only; they do not replace Lattice CLI/test evidence.

verificationEvidence.command: lattice validate --story=B-e3d9 before adding CHK-005 evidence
verificationEvidence.note: The pre-evidence validate run passed npm test but still refused completion with 12/15 covered and CHK-005 missing, proving host transcripts or partial command success cannot satisfy the gate without current Lattice verificationEvidence.
